scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for the older brother to let his 7-year-old brother stay up late. Let me break this down step by step. First, the older brother is 18, and he's in charge of his 7-year-old brother while their mom is out until 1 AM. The younger brother is sensitive to sleep, meaning if he doesn't get enough, he gets cranky the next day. The older brother made sure his brother went to bed on time, but then his friend came over, and they were watching a movie and being loud. The younger brother woke up and wanted to join them. The older brother told him to go back to bed, but his friend encouraged letting him stay. The older brother was worried that if he tried to make his brother go back to bed, it would lead to a tantrum and be embarrassing or exhausting. So, he let his brother stay, and by the end of the movie, his brother was asleep. The next morning, the younger brother was cranky and didn't want to get up, even though it was the weekend. The mom found out and got mad at the older brother. The older brother thinks that since his brother is 7, he should understand consequences and that staying up late would make him feel bad. He also mentioned that two hours of missed sleep isn't a big deal. So, is the older brother AITA (Ask if it's a Thing, AKA overreacting or being unreasonable) for not forcing his brother to go to bed? Let me think about the different aspects here. On one hand, the older brother was trying to manage the situation without causing a big scene. He was concerned about the potential tantrum and the effort it would take to get his brother back to bed. On the other hand, the younger brother is sensitive to sleep, and missing two hours could have a noticeable impact on his mood and behavior the next day. I also need to consider the role of the older brother. At 18, he's responsible for his younger sibling, but he's also entertaining his friend. There's a balance between being a responsible caretaker and having some downtime with friends. It's understandable that he didn't want to ruin the evening with his friend by dealing with a tantrum. However, the younger brother is only 7, and while he can put himself to bed, he's still a child who might not fully grasp the long-term consequences of missing sleep. The older brother's reasoning that two hours isn't a big deal might be valid, but it's also about consistency and teaching responsibility. If the younger brother learns that he can stay up late when he wants, it might set a precedent for future behavior. Another angle is the reaction from the mom. She got mad at the older brother, which indicates that she expects him to enforce the bedtime rules, even if it's inconvenient. This could be a point of conflict between the siblings and the parent. In terms of whether it's right or wrong, it seems like a gray area. The older brother was trying to avoid a difficult situation, but he also had a responsibility to ensure his brother got enough sleep. It's possible that he could have handled it differently, like setting a firm but kind boundary with his brother, explaining that it's important to get enough sleep so he feels good the next day. That way, he teaches his brother about consequences without causing a tantrum. Alternatively, maybe the older brother could have found a compromise, like letting his brother stay up for a little while longer but ensuring he still gets enough sleep. Or perhaps he could have involved his friend in helping to enforce the bedtime, making it a team effort. Overall, while the older brother's intentions were good, not enforcing the bedtime might have been a missed opportunity to teach his brother about responsibility and consequences. However, it's also important to consider the effort and stress involved in managing a young child's behavior, especially when trying to have some time with friends. So, in conclusion, it's a bit of both. The older brother wasn't entirely wrong for wanting to avoid a tantrum, but there could have been a better way to handle the situation that still respects the importance of sleep and teaches his brother about consequences.
